audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart read Skill for rows 0-5 while the content layer and the packet chart both read Karma/Karma/Skill/Skill/Viktor/Viktor/Viktor. The page rendered two different answers to who wins Level 1.
audit.why: Inner Flame (Q) has 950 range against Siphon Power's 600 and Hextech Ray's 525, and Viktor's Hex Fragments come from kills, so Karma genuinely owns levels 1-2. Viktor takes over at 6 with Arcane Storm (120/100/80s) and again at his first item.
audit.corrected: Full-layer phases[0..5].side aligned to the content layer, with every why rewritten in the same proposal to match the new verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike prose used outdated/fabricated ability names — 'Chaos Storm', 'Power Siphon', 'Death Ray' — and claimed Viktor farms his passive stacks.
audit.why: Riot's kit text names them Arcane Storm (R), Siphon Power (Q) and Hextech Ray (E), and the passive grants Hex Fragments on kills, not on farm.
audit.corrected: Spikes and early/mid/late rewritten on real names, with Gravity Field's 13s maxed cooldown and Arcane Storm's 120s giving the spikes concrete timings.

audit.whatIsWrong: No ability-by-ability interaction was stated anywhere; breakdown.cooldowns contained no number at all (lintFindings COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: The decisive interaction is a range war: Karma's Inner Flame (950) and Focused Resolve (675) versus Siphon Power (600), Hextech Ray (525) and Gravity Field (800, 17/16/15/14/13s). Viktor's Siphon Power is an auto-attack reset, so his wind-up — not his cast — is the tell to step back.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries Gravity Field 17s/13s, Hextech Ray 12s at 60 mana, and Arcane Storm 120s; dos/donts bodies reground on those numbers.

audit.why: Gravity Field is the gate on every all-in and it is down for 17s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns now say wait for Gravity Field to drop, then RQ his step-up.

audit.whatIsWrong: The brief's missingInteractions asserts Arcane Storm is a channel that Focused Resolve/Mantra cancels.
audit.why: Riot's own description says Arcane Storm interrupts enemy channels; it does not describe Viktor channelling. The derived 'channel' flag contradicts the description, so per the brief's rule I trust the description and did not write the claim.

edits.after: Mantra spent on a wave is an RQ not spent on Viktor, and his lane only strengthens while your window closes.

edits.before: A scaled Viktor with full Hex Core stacks and Death Ray poke simply out-damages Karma's kit in every extended fight, and his R zone denies your positioning entirely.
edits.after: A scaled Viktor with every ability augmented and Hextech Ray poke out-damages Karma's kit in every extended fight, and Arcane Storm denies your positioning entirely.

edits.before: The moment Viktor hits 6, Chaos Storm gives him a skirmish-winning tool, and once his Hex Core evolves shortly after his Gravity Field zones you out of poke range and his scaling damage output starts outpacing your sustained poke.
edits.after: The moment Viktor hits 6, Arcane Storm gives him a skirmish tool he can redirect, and once his abilities augment, Gravity Field on a 13-second cooldown zones you out of poke range and his damage outpaces your poke.

edits.before: A completed Viktor with augmented abilities and Death Ray simply deals more raw damage than Karma can shield away, and his R zone control wins teamfights outright regardless of your utility.
edits.after: A completed Viktor with augmented abilities and Hextech Ray deals more raw damage than Karma can shield away, and Arcane Storm wins teamfights outright regardless of your utility.

edits.before: Use Mantra-R shield proactively before his Death Ray poke lands
edits.after: Use the Mantra-E shield proactively before his Hextech Ray poke lands

edits.before: Viktor is genuinely weak before his items click — his passive needs stacks and his poke damage is low, so Karma's superior range and shield let you push an early lead through level 5 comfortably.
edits.after: Viktor is weak before his items click — Hex Fragments come from kills and Siphon Power only reaches 600, so Inner Flame at 950 and the Inspire shield build you a lead through level 5.
